lead.label: 7I
lead.why: We found one compound, 7I, that is more active than the parent compound, LQZ-7, and when given orally effectively inhibits xenograft tumor growth ... 7I ... can be used as a lead for further optimization

reactions.conditions: General procedure for 7I/7J (method A): 2,3-dichloroquinoxaline (1.0 equiv), 4-fluoroaniline (2.2 equiv; two molecules are incorporated), EtOH (0.2 M), reflux 16 h; EtOAc/water workup; column chromatography; 52% yield
reactions.source: Main article, Chemical Synthesis and Methods (page 8-10 of the accepted manuscript) and the 7I characterisation paragraph; Figure 1C; SI is figures only

notes: Two aniline molecules are incorporated (symmetric double SNAr), listed once. The text contradicts itself on the starting material: the prose says '1,4-dihydro-2,3-quinoxalinedione (1)' while the experimental says 'commercially available 2,3-dichloroquinoxaline (1)' (chlorines are lost in the reaction; the experimental reading is chemically sensible and used here). Alternative reading with quinoxalinedione is not used because ethanol reflux with anilines would not displace a dione oxygen.
